events.excerpt: TL;DR On an 8 GB M2 running leanVM at commit df7d122, hash-based accumulation did not beat leanVM’s full-verifier recursion inside an aggregator. Our best batching design also missed its 15% gate once the leaf size was tuned. Negative results (D1, D2, D3-S). Folding leanXMSS verifications directly needs at least 7.1M R1CS constraints per signature. That is about 450x leanVM’s per-signature cost (Inferred from measured WARP rates). Folding the whole leanVM step relation runs at 260 ns per witness element, against leanVM’s 55 ns per committed word (Verified rates). Accumulating children’s openings across merges spends about 57k cycles per step to save at most 46k (Verified counts). Cost anatomy (Verified). Verifying one child inside a merge costs 186.8k VM cycles. Its WHIR opening is 55% of that. Merkle hashing is 12% of the cycles but 79% of the Keccak calls. 73% of the JUMP rows are subfield checks. Batched child openings (B’-L1). One shared WHIR opening from level 1 saves 32.8k cycles per child (17.6%, Verified by cost emulation). A round-by-round sketch keeps leanVM’s bounds (Inferred). For 1,500 signatures it is still 2.4% slower at the slot deadline than the baseline at the baseline’s best configuration. Configuration rule (Verified on this machine). A merge node that steps from mu 25 to mu 26 takes 1.4 to 1.8x longer for about 3% more committed words. Aggregating 1,500 signatures as 5 leaves of 300 instead of 6 of 250 keeps the node at mu 25. The deadline drops from 3.11 s to 2.24 s and CPU per slot from 7.99 s to 6.47 s. A cost model that is linear in fan-in and leaf
